oneOf.description: Its owner, as if they'd sent it.
A chat, as if sent there.

agent-state-protocol.destination-owner.description: Its owner, as if they'd sent it.

connection.description:
The connection of the owner's direct chat it comes from
(`slack`); left out, the CLI inbox.

kind.description: Where it goes: its owner, on a connection or the CLI inbox, or a thread.

agent-state-protocol.destination-thread.description: A chat, as if sent there.

kind.description: Where it goes: its owner, on a connection or the CLI inbox, or a thread.

thread.description:
The chat, by its connection and its id there
(`slack:C0TEAM`).

oneOf.description: On a cron line's times, in a zone.
Every so many seconds, counted from an anchor.

at.description: The Unix time, in seconds, it fires.

kind.description: Which timing it is: cron, every so many seconds, or once at a time.

agent-state-protocol.when-cron.description: On a cron line's times, in a zone.

cron.description:
Five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month and day of
the week (`0 9 * * 1-5`).

kind.description: Which timing it is: cron, every so many seconds, or once at a time.

zone.description: The IANA time zone its times are in (`Europe/London`).

agent-state-protocol.when-every.description: Every so many seconds, counted from an anchor.

anchor.description: The Unix time, in seconds, its firings are counted from.

kind.description: Which timing it is: cron, every so many seconds, or once at a time.

seconds.description: How many seconds apart, at least one.

agent.agent-chat.description:
A chat on a connection, whoever is in it, `chat:<connection>:<id>`:
a group the connection keeps, which a specification lets message its agent,
never a principal. Its id is the connection's own (Slack's `C0TEAM`,
Telegram's `-1001234`).

agent.agent-code-server.description:
A language server of code's (`[tool.code.servers.<language>]`). Each
key is its own in a specification's union, so a specification may change one alone: a
key left out is the specification before's.

command.description:
The program and its arguments, as `run` would start them; empty,
no server for the language.

files.description: The files it serves, by their extension (`rs`).

roots.description:
The files that mark a project's root (`Cargo.toml`): the nearest
folder above a file that holds one is the root its server is
started in; none found, the files folder.

additionalProperties.description: A section of the server's settings, as the server reads it

settings.description:
The server's settings, by the section it asks for
(`rust-analyzer`): given whole when it asks for its configuration,
and told once it starts. Left out, it has its own defaults.

agent.agent-commands.description:
Its commands: a message of its owner's that names one (`/new`) runs
it in place of a turn. Each is on when it's true here; left out, off.

ask.description: `/chat:ask`: a question answered apart, nothing kept.

compact.description: `/chat:compact`: what's before the last message summarized now.

create.description: `/new`: a new conversation in the same chat.

export.description: `/chat:export`: this conversation written to a file.

fork.description: `/chat:fork`: a conversation holding this one as it stands.

goal.description:
`/goal`: a goal it pursues after each answer until it holds,
within `[goals]`' limits.

model.description: `/model`: the model, or a switch to another of its provider's.

models.description: `/models`: the models offered by its provider.

queue.description: `/chat:queue`: the next message waits for the running turn.

resume.description: `/chat:resume`: the chat's conversations, or one taken up again.

status.description: `/status`: the model and what the conversation holds.

steer.description:
`/chat:steer`: the next message joins the running turn, where
`[turns] busy` steers.

tasks.description: `/tasks` and `/ps`: its running and scheduled work.

verbose.description: `/chat:verbose`: whether the chat shows each tool call.

write.description:
`/learn`: a skill written from what it just did, where it may
write `skills/` with its file tool.

agent.agent-compact-at.description: When a conversation is compacted (`[window] compact_at`): once it fills this share of what the window holds of it, or `never`.

oneOf.description: Once it fills this share of what the window holds of it

agent.agent-extends.description: What a specification starts from. `link`, link's specification, as when it's left out; `none`, nothing: every key is the file's own.

agent.agent-goals.description:
How long a goal is pursued, turn after turn, before it's left:
whichever is reached first.

tokens.description:
The most tokens those turns spend, its prompts' and answers', at least
1000: Link's specification sets 1000000.

turns.description:
The most turns it takes on its own toward a goal, after the one that set
it, from 1 to 1000. Link's specification sets 10.

name.description:
The harness's name, as `lnk agent harness list` names it (`link`,
`openclaw`): lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

agent.agent-instructions.description:
What it's told to be: one file, nothing, or Link's sections. With
Link's assembly, where each section of its prompt comes from,
and how large each may be. A section's source is `link` (Link's own),
`none`, or a file in the agent's files folder (`instructions/base.md`).
The model's and the tools' have no source: its file in
`instructions/models/` and what each tool says of itself, so only
their most is set. The repository's is `link` (its `AGENTS.md` files)
or `none`.

base.description:
The prompt's first section, what any agent of yours is: `link` (Link's,
a personal agent who answers briefly), `none`, or a file in its files
(`instructions/base.md`). Link's specification sets `"link"`.

environment.description:
The fourth section, what it runs with here as Link resolved it at its
start: where its files are, which folders it may change, its
connections; `link`, `none` or a file. Link's specification sets `"link"`.

notes.description:
The ninth section, what the agent noted for itself, the file its
memory's `remember` writes, read at each message, or `none`. Link's specification
sets `"memory/notes.md"`; the old `instructions/notes.md` reads as it.

now.description:
The date, the time here, the connection and who's speaking, at the head
of each message, never in the system prompt: `link` or `none`. Link's
specification sets `"link"`.

owner.description:
The seventh section, who you are (your name, your work, the people in
your life, how you like things): a file of yours in its files, read at
each message, or `none`. Link's specification sets `"instructions/owner.md"`.

persona.description:
The sixth section, who it is apart from any task (its name, its voice,
its character): a file of yours in its files, read at each message, or
`none`. Link's specification sets `"instructions/persona.md"`.

skills.description:
The fifth section, each skill's name and what it's for, from
`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in its files, sorted by name; `link`, `none` or
a file. Link's specification sets `"link"`.

source.description:
The whole prompt's source: `"link"`, as left out, assembles the sections
below; a Markdown file in the agent's files
(`"instructions/instruction.md"`) supplies the whole system prompt, read
again each turn without headings, templates, model overrides or message
times; `"none"` supplies none.

A file is read up to 64 KB, its outer whitespace trimmed; a missing,
empty or linked one supplies nothing. Section sources and sizes hold
only with `"link"`, and with `extends = "none"` a file or `"none"` needs
no section keys. Only a harness whose contract takes instructions, as
Link Harness does, takes the table: a start refuses it for any other.

standing.description:
The eighth section, your standing instructions: a file in its files it
may edit, read at each message, or `none`. Link's specification sets
`"instructions/instruction.md"`.

agent.agent-isolation.description:
An agent specification's `[isolation]`: the VM a new agent is made in, its
only key a specification may set.

vm.description:
The VM specification a new agent is made in, relative to this file. This
build has no VM provider, so a specification naming one is refused, never
run in a sandbox instead.
vm.x-link-unavailable: this build of Link has no VM provider

agent.agent-late.description: What a firing missed while the machine slept does. `run`, it fires once, on waking; `skip`, it doesn't; a recurring one fires at its next time.

agent.agent-message-access.description:
An agent specification's `[access]`: who besides its owner may message it.
It takes chats alone, so a team's `member` isn't one of its keys.

message.description:
Who may message the agent, besides its owner: chats on its
connections, whoever is in them, each `chat:<connection>:<chat
id>` (`chat:slack:C0TEAM`).

items.description:
A chat on a connection, whoever is in it, `chat:<connection>:<id>`:
a group the connection keeps, which a specification lets message its agent,
never a principal. Its id is the connection's own (Slack's `C0TEAM`,
Telegram's `-1001234`).

agent.agent-model.description: The model, and how it's asked.

aliases.description:
Names for models, each a word for a model as its provider names it
(`high = "claude-opus-5-5"`): `/model:set high`, a subagent started on
`high` and a fallback of `high` each run that model. Only `[model]`
takes the table, never a provider's, and Link's specification has none.

allow.description: The only models it may run; left out, any.

answer.description:
The longest answer, in tokens, as you set it, at least 256; left out,
`[window] answer`'s share of the window, at most the model's own.

anthropic.description:
A provider's table of `[model]`: the keys that differ by provider,
each replacing `[model]`'s for an agent thinking with one of its
models. It holds no tables of its own.

default.description:
The model when the agent names none.

In `[model]`, named with who serves it (`local/qwen3:8b`,
`anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`); in a provider's table, as that provider
names it. Link's specification sets `claude-haiku-5-5` on Anthropic, `gpt-6-luna`
on OpenAI and `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` on OpenRouter. `lnk agent
start --model.default <model>` selects it for the agent.

fallback.description:
Whether a turn its model can't answer goes to the fallback model,
`fallback_model`: the model is off, the turn's prompt is past its
window, or its provider is busy (429, or a 5xx). False, it fails,
and the agent keeps no fallback.

fallback_model.description:
The hosted model used when falling back, named as `default` names
one (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`), or one of `aliases`. Its
credential is its provider's, or `LNK_FALLBACK_CREDENTIAL`'s. Link
Harness falls back; a harness that can't says so.

local.description:
A provider's table of `[model]`: the keys that differ by provider,
each replacing `[model]`'s for an agent thinking with one of its
models. It holds no tables of its own.

ollama.description:
A provider's table of `[model]`: the keys that differ by provider,
each replacing `[model]`'s for an agent thinking with one of its
models. It holds no tables of its own.

openai.description:
A provider's table of `[model]`: the keys that differ by provider,
each replacing `[model]`'s for an agent thinking with one of its
models. It holds no tables of its own.

openrouter.description:
A provider's table of `[model]`: the keys that differ by provider,
each replacing `[model]`'s for an agent thinking with one of its
models. It holds no tables of its own.

thinking.description: How hard a model thinks: `off`, `low`, `medium` or `high`.

thinking_budget.description:
The most tokens it thinks, at least 1024, for a model that thinks within
a budget. Link's specification sets 2048.

transcribe.description:
The model of its provider a voice note is heard with, its words the
message's (`[connections] voice`); left out, or `"none"`, a voice note
is left out, and the agent told so. Link's specification sets OpenAI's
`gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`.

agent.agent-provider-model.description:
A provider's table of `[model]`: the keys that differ by provider,
each replacing `[model]`'s for an agent thinking with one of its
models. It holds no tables of its own.

allow.description: The only models of this provider it may run; left out, `[model]`'s.

answer.description: The longest answer, in tokens, at least 256.

default.description:
The model when the agent names none, as this provider names it
(`claude-sonnet-5-5`).

thinking.description: How hard a model thinks: `off`, `low`, `medium` or `high`.

thinking_budget.description:
The most tokens it thinks, at least 1024, for a model that thinks
within a budget.

transcribe.description:
The model of this provider a voice note is heard with; `"none"`,
none.

agent.agent-run.description: How an agent runs on its machine (`[run]`).

files.description:
The agent's workspace folder. A relative path is from the folder the
start runs in; left out, it keeps the workspace it has. `lnk agent start
--run.files <dir>` sets it.

idle_after.description:
How long it goes with no message, no turn and no background command
before it stops, holding no process, memory or port, started again by
its next message: at least `"1s"`, or `"never"`, memory kept against a
start from cold. Link's specification sets `"5m"`.

It holds only where the machine's `shared_bridge` is on
(`~/.lnk/safe/agents/policy.toml`), since the
bridge then listens for it, and for an agent whose harness speaks none
of its connections itself.

let_sleep.description:
Whether the machine may sleep while this agent runs: left out or false,
the agent keeps it awake; true, the machine's own sleep policy applies.

agent.agent-schedule.description:
A schedule the agent keeps: a message sent to it at a time, as if
from where it goes.

enabled.description: Whether it fires; false keeps it, firing nothing.

message.description: The message the agent is sent when it fires.

name.description:
Its name, unique among the agent's schedules, which its record
knows it by.

agent.agent-scheduler-driver.description:
What wakes the scheduler's runner. `service`, the agent's bridge, a background service, runs it for good; `cron`, the machine's calendar (launchd on a mac, cron elsewhere) starts
it once a minute; nothing of it runs between; `address`, a machine that runs the agent only while it answers: the
scheduler tells it, at the address the machine gives, when the
agent's jobs are next due, and whatever wakes the agent then runs
it once; nothing of it runs between.

agent.agent-scheduler-recurring.description:
The scheduler's: whether a recurring schedule the agent makes asks you
first. `ask`, it waits for you to allow it unless its call says once;
`allow`, it starts without asking, as a one-off reminder does, though
`ask = true` still asks first of every call that writes. Link's specification
sets `ask`.

base.description: The base section: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's cut.

environment.description: What it runs with here: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's cut.

model.description:
The model's own section, the second, from
`instructions/models/<maker>/<model>/instruction.md` in its files: its
most, past which it's cut. It has no source key.

notes.description:
What the agent noted for itself: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's
cut.

now.description:
The date, connection and speaker at the head of each message: its most
(`"16 KB"`), past which it's cut.

owner.description: Who its owner is: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's cut.

persona.description: Who it is: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's cut.

repository.description:
What the repository it works in says of itself: its most (`"16 KB"`),
past which it's cut.

skills.description: Its skills: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's cut.

standing.description:
What its owner tells it to be: its most (`"16 KB"`), past which it's
cut.

tools.description:
The tools' section, the third, what each tool says of itself: its most,
past which tools are cut whole. It has no source key.

additionalProperties.description: A key of a tool from outside Link, its own to read: Link keeps it and doesn't read it

agent.agent-tool.description:
A tool's opinions (`[tools]` for every tool, `[tool.<name>]` for one).
Link's tools' keys are typed; a tool from outside Link may have keys
of its own ([`Tool::other`]).

answer.description:
What's kept of a tool's answer, 1 KB to 16 MB; in `[tool.<name>]`, one
tool's. Link's specification sets `"32 KB"`.

ask.description:
The scheduler's: whether every call but those that only read asks you
first. A recurring schedule asks you either way, unless its call says
once or `recurring` is `allow`. Link's specification sets false.

background.description:
Run's: the most background commands at once, 0 to 64; 0, none. Link's
specification sets 4.

background_keep.description:
Run's: how long a background command's record and output stay once it
ended and the agent was told, 1m to 365d. Link's specification sets `"1d"`.

background_output.description:
Run's: what's kept on disk of a background command's output, its end, 1
KB to 1 GB. Link's specification sets `"16 MB"`.

background_per_day.description:
Run's: the most background commands started in a day, each of whose
endings starts a turn, 1 to 65535. Link's specification sets 100.

background_timeout.description:
Run's: the longest a background command runs before it's stopped, 1s to
7d. Link's specification sets `"1h"`.

deadline.description:
Memory's: how long a search ranks before it answers with what it has.
Link's specification sets `"300ms"`.

diffs.description:
File's: whether `write` and `replace` answer with the change as a diff.
A feature's switch, off when left out.

dimensions.description:
Memory's: how many of the embedding model's dimensions are kept: fewer
cost less memory and disk, more rank a little better. Link's
specification sets 256.

driver.description:
What wakes the scheduler's runner. `service`, the agent's bridge, a background service, runs it for good; `cron`, the machine's calendar (launchd on a mac, cron elsewhere) starts
it once a minute; nothing of it runs between; `address`, a machine that runs the agent only while it answers: the
scheduler tells it, at the address the machine gives, when the
agent's jobs are next due, and whatever wakes the agent then runs
it once; nothing of it runs between.

enabled.description:
Whether Link starts the tool for the agent, in `[tool.scheduler]`,
`[tool.run]`, `[tool.file]`, `[tool.code]` and `[tool.mcp]`; false
withholds it. Link's specification starts every tool disabled: the file tool, the
scheduler, run, code and Link MCP. Without the scheduler, no subagents or
schedules run. `[tool.browser]` and `[tool.desktop]` take it too: true
gives the screen at a start where this machine runs it, false takes it
away, and Link's specification says neither, leaving what `lnk agent tool add`
gave.

fetch.description:
Web's: the most of a page one fetch gives, 1 KB to 1 MB; each part says
where the next starts. Link's specification sets `"24 KB"`.

file.description:
Memory's: the largest file in its folders it indexes; a larger one is
left out, and a search's reply names it. Link's specification sets
`"16 MB"`.

find.description:
File's: whether it finds files by name and lines by a pattern (`find`).
A feature's switch, off when left out.

firing.description:
The scheduler's: how long it waits on a firing, a subagent's whole work,
before it gives up on it, 1s to 1d. Link's specification sets `"30m"`.

folders.description:
Memory's: the agent's folders it indexes, `memory` (its Home's) and
`chats` (its conversations). Link's specification sets both.

hops.description:
The scheduler's: how deep a chain of messages goes, each sent by an
agent on its own, from 1: a depth and not a count, as a recurring job's
firings start again. Link's specification sets 8.

hosts.description:
Web's: the only hosts it fetches, as `[internet] hosts` names them: a
name (`docs.rs`), `*.` and a name for every name under it, or an
address; each redirect is held to them too. Left out, it fetches any
public host, as Link's specification leaves it. Link Harness sends it with each
call.

keep.description:
Memory's: how long its session stays once no turn uses it. Link's specification
sets `"10m"`.

kept_off.description:
Memory's: the largest index kept off the machine, fetched at each wake
where the machine runs agents only while they answer. Link's
specification sets `"2 GB"`.

late.description: What a firing missed while the machine slept does. `run`, it fires once, on waking; `skip`, it doesn't; a recurring one fires at its next time.

max_age.description: Memory's: how long its session lives at most. Link's specification sets `"1h"`.

memory.description:
Memory's: the most its service holds of its own for this agent's index,
besides the pages of files it maps. Link's specification sets
`"512 MB"`.

model.description:
Memory's: the embedding model it ranks by; `none`, by words only, no
model started. Link's specification sets `qwen3-embedding`.

notes.description:
Memory's: how large the agent's notes may grow, 64 B to 64 KB, past
which `remember` refuses to write. Link's specification sets `"4 KB"`.

output.description:
Run's: what's kept of each of a command's output and its errors, its
start and its end, 1 KB to 16 MB. Link's specification sets `"16 KB"`.

per_day.description:
The scheduler's: messages its schedules send the agent a day, the day
in its `zone`, from 1; subagents' work is outside it. It bounds how many
messages agents send each other, and caps what the agent takes from each
teammate a day (UTC). Link's specification sets 100.

program.description:
The browser's: the Chromium-family program it starts, by its absolute
path, in place of the one it finds on this machine. It's an executable
program, never a launcher script (a file starting with `#!`), which
would run inside the browser's sandbox and be refused the programs it
calls; each start checks it, and refuses one that isn't. Left out, the
browser finds one, as Link's specification leaves it.

recurring.description:
The scheduler's: whether a recurring schedule the agent makes asks you
first. `ask`, it waits for you to allow it unless its call says once;
`allow`, it starts without asking, as a one-off reminder does, though
`ask = true` still asks first of every call that writes. Link's specification
sets `ask`.

reserve.description:
Memory's: the disk left free; below it indexing pauses, calls go on
answering, and it resumes once there's room. Link's specification sets
`"1 GB"`.

additionalProperties.description:
A language server of code's (`[tool.code.servers.<language>]`). Each
key is its own in a specification's union, so a specification may change one alone: a
key left out is the specification before's.

servers.description:
Code's: the language servers it may start, by the language each
serves (`rust`).

strangers.description:
`[tools]` only: the tools a stranger's message may use, by the
names the harness offers them (`web__fetch`), its conversation
given these or fewer ([`crate::access::Standing::Stranger`]). Left
out, none.

subagents.description: The scheduler's: subagents at work at once, from 1. Link's specification sets 5.

threads.description:
Memory's: the threads indexing takes, so a laptop isn't
taken over. Link's specification sets 1.

timeout.description:
How long a tool's call may take, at least a second; past it the model is
told it didn't answer. In `[tool.<name>]`, one tool's: the run tool
stops a command a tenth before it (2 s at least, half at most), with
all it started, so what it printed comes back. Waiting for you to allow a call isn't counted: a
tool not Link's own has `[connections] ask_wait` beside it. Link's specification
sets `"5m"`, and the run tool's `"2m"`.

tokens.description:
Memory's: the most tokens a search or a read gives, at least 100 and at
most 6000, the most one answer holds. Link's specification sets 6000.

zone.description:
The scheduler's: the time zone its times are in, `local` (this
machine's) or a zone's name (`Europe/Paris`). Link's specification sets `local`.

agent.agent-turns.description: How long a turn may go on.

busy.description: What a message sent while a turn runs does. `queue`, it gets a turn of its own after; `steer`, it joins the running turn, at its next round; `interrupt`, the running turn ends now, and it gets a turn of its own.

calls.description: The most calls one answer makes, from 1. Link's specification sets 16.

lapse.description:
How long a lease not renewed lasts before its turn is taken for crashed
and finished, more than twice `renew`. Link's specification sets `"60s"`.

renew.description:
How often a running turn renews its lease, at least `"1s"`. Link's specification
sets `"10s"`.

rounds.description: The most rounds of calls in one turn, from 1. Link's specification sets 8.

agent.agent-window.description: How much of the model's window a turn fills.

answer.description:
The share of the window kept for the answer, over 0 and under 1 and
under 1 with `margin`, at most the model's longest, where `[model]
answer` doesn't say. Link's specification sets 0.25.

compact_at.description: When a conversation is compacted (`[window] compact_at`): once it fills this share of what the window holds of it, or `never`.

margin.description:
The share of the window kept back, from 0 to under 0.5: tokens are
counted roughly before a turn, exactly by the provider after (`0.125`,
an eighth). Link's specification sets 0.125.

max.description:
The window a turn fills, in tokens, at least 1024: yours or a team's as
set, Link's held to the model's own window; left out, the model's whole
window. Link's specification sets 128000.

past_price_jump.description:
Whether a turn fills the window past its model's first price jump, where
a long prompt costs more (the model's facts' `above`, as `lnk model
show` prints them).

False fills the window only up to that size, `max` included, so the
conversation compacts within it; true fills the whole window, each call
past the jump at its higher price. Link's specification sets false.

save_notes.description:
Whether, before it compacts, the model is asked to save what matters to
its notes, where it has a tool to (`memory__remember`), in a
conversation you spoke in, never one of others' messages alone. Link's
specification sets true.

unknown.description:
The window of a model Link doesn't know, in tokens, at least 1024.
Link's specification sets 32768.

connection-policy.activity.description:
How each tool it calls shows, a line each with what it works on
(`› file read: notes/plan.md`, `› run command: cargo test`), where its
harness tells its calls (ACP's `tool_call`), as Link Harness does:
`replace`, above the answer being written, the latest eight, the
finished answer then shown alone; `keep`, the same, every line staying
above the finished answer as a log; or `off`, none. Link's specification sets
`replace`; `/chat:verbose` turns it off and on for one conversation.

connection-policy.connection.description:
A connection's opinions (`[connections]` for every connection, `[connection.<name>]`
for one).

activity.description:
How each tool it calls shows, a line each with what it works on
(`› file read: notes/plan.md`, `› run command: cargo test`), where its
harness tells its calls (ACP's `tool_call`), as Link Harness does:
`replace`, above the answer being written, the latest eight, the
finished answer then shown alone; `keep`, the same, every line staying
above the finished answer as a log; or `off`, none. Link's specification sets
`replace`; `/chat:verbose` turns it off and on for one conversation.

activity_mark.description:
What leads each tool call's line (`"›"`): empty (`""`), nothing.
Link's specification sets `"›"`.

activity_separator.description:
What stands between a tool call and what it works on (`": "`), as
`› run command: git commit`; a call with nothing to show it works
on shows none (`› web search`). Link's specification sets `": "`.

ask_wait.description:
How long a question for you waits for your answer, a call of a tool that
asks first or a page to open, a second to a day: no answer in time is
no, and a tool's call has its own `timeout` beside it. `[connections]`'s
alone, since a question waits as long on every connection. Link's specification
sets `"10m"`.

cache.description:
How long its provider's cache is asked to keep a conversation's
prompt: `"auto"`, the lifetime expected to cost least, or one the
provider offers (`"1h"`). Link's specification sets `"auto"`.

compact_after.description:
When a quiet conversation on it is compacted by time: `"auto"`, just
before its cache ends when that costs less than reading it again; a
time of quiet, at least `"1m"`; or `"never"`. It needs the `scheduler`
tool. Link's specification sets `"auto"`, and `"never"` for `link`.

documents.description:
Whether a message's documents (PDF or text) reach the agent; false
or left out, each is left out and the agent told so.

groups.description: Which of the owner's messages in a group an agent answers. `mention`, those that mention it, or answer one of its messages; `never`, none: it talks in direct messages only.

images.description:
Whether a message's images reach the agent; false or left out,
each is left out and the agent told so.

pace.description:
How often an answer being written is shown again, over 0; never more
often than the platform documents a bot may write: Telegram once a
second in a chat and every 3 seconds in a group, Slack every 1.2
seconds, and Discord its global 50 requests a second and the limits it
answers with. Told by the platform to wait, Telegram and Slack show
nothing more until then, and only the finished answer waits and tries
again. Link's specification sets `"1s"`.

pauses.description:
What `"auto"` assumes of a new conversation's pauses, each counted as
one it saw. Link's specification sets a chat's to `["1m", "1m", "20m", "8h"]`.

steered.description:
A reaction on a message that joined a running turn ([`Busy::Steer`]),
where the connection has them; empty (`""`) or left out, none.

stream.description:
The answer shown as it's written; false, once it's done. Link's specification
sets true.

voice.description:
Whether a message's voice notes reach the agent, heard as their
words by its provider (`[model] transcribe`); false or left out,
each is left out and the agent told so.

working.description:
A reaction on your message while it answers, by its name (`"eyes"`),
where the connection has them; empty (`""`) or left out, none. Of
Link's connections Slack and Discord mark a message, so it's refused
for Telegram and Signal; Discord knows the names its
`reactions.toml` lists. Link's `[connection.slack]` and
`[connection.discord]` set `"eyes"`.

connection-policy.groups.description: Which of the owner's messages in a group an agent answers. `mention`, those that mention it, or answer one of its messages; `never`, none: it talks in direct messages only.

harness-wire.busy.description: What a message sent while a turn runs does. `queue`, it gets a turn of its own after; `steer`, it joins the running turn, at its next round; `interrupt`, the running turn ends now, and it gets a turn of its own.

interactions.domain-id.description: A domain of questions (`tool.approval`): letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `:`, `-` or `/`, at most 256 of them.

allow_request_overrides.description: Whether the asker's own wait and fallbacks replace these.

choice.description: What a question left unanswered becomes. `expire`, nothing: it expires unanswered; `use_default`, its default answer; `use_recommended`, its recommended answer.

confirmation.description: What a question left unanswered becomes. `expire`, nothing: it expires unanswered; `use_default`, its default answer; `use_recommended`, its recommended answer.

text.description: What a question left unanswered becomes. `expire`, nothing: it expires unanswered; `use_default`, its default answer; `use_recommended`, its recommended answer.

wait_secs.description:
How long a question waits for an answer, in seconds, at most a
day.

interactions.fallback.description: What a question left unanswered becomes. `expire`, nothing: it expires unanswered; `use_default`, its default answer; `use_recommended`, its recommended answer.

domains.description:
How long a question of each kind waits for its owner, and what an
unanswered one becomes, by its domain (`tool.approval`). A domain's
opinion holds for the domains below it unless theirs says.

propertyNames.description: A domain of questions (`tool.approval`): letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `:`, `-` or `/`, at most 256 of them.

model.thinking.description: How hard a model thinks: `off`, `low`, `medium` or `high`.

store.storage.description:
Where an agent would keep each of its collections (its specification's
`[storage]`): a place's name each, a request its machine has the
last word on. A harness from outside Link keeps its own conversations
however it does.

conversations.description:
Where a new conversation is kept: a place (`file`
or a driver's name, `sqlite` the program `lnk-sqlite-store`,
a store), or `log` or `compact`,
each `file`. A conversation already kept is read
where it is: `lnk agent chat export --format` converts it.

home.description:
Where it would keep its home, the person's documents and work (`Home/`):
a place's name, lowercase letters, digits and dashes. It's a request:
the machine's `[storage]` has the last word, and a place it doesn't
support gets its default. Link's specification sets `"file"`.

instructions.description:
Where it would keep its instructions, which you edit. It's a request:
the machine's `[storage]` has the last word, and a place it doesn't
support gets its default. Link's specification sets `"file"`.

memory.description:
Where it would keep memory's notes and index. It's a request: the
machine's `[storage]` has the last word, and a place it doesn't support
gets its default. Link's specification sets `"file"`.

schedule.description:
Where it would keep its scheduled jobs. It's a request: the machine's
`[storage]` has the last word, and a place it doesn't support gets its
default. Link's specification sets `"file"`.

skills.description:
Where it would keep its skills, which you edit. It's a request: the
machine's `[storage]` has the last word, and a place it doesn't support
gets its default. Link's specification sets `"file"`.

description:
An agent, written down: the file `lnk agent start --spec` reads and
`lnk agent spec show` prints.

access.description:
An agent specification's `[access]`: who besides its owner may message it.
It takes chats alone, so a team's `member` isn't one of its keys.

command_response.description: Text shown before a command's harness answer; empty disables it.

commands.description:
Its commands: a message of its owner's that names one (`/new`) runs
it in place of a turn. Each is on when it's true here; left out, off.

additionalProperties.description:
A connection's opinions (`[connections]` for every connection, `[connection.<name>]`
for one).

connection.description: Each connection's own, by its module's name (`slack`).

connections.description:
A connection's opinions (`[connections]` for every connection, `[connection.<name>]`
for one).

env.description: Environment input for future agent creation, relative to this file.

extends.description: What a specification starts from. `link`, link's specification, as when it's left out; `none`, nothing: every key is the file's own.

goals.description:
How long a goal is pursued, turn after turn, before it's left:
whichever is reached first.

instructions.description:
What it's told to be: one file, nothing, or Link's sections. With
Link's assembly, where each section of its prompt comes from,
and how large each may be. A section's source is `link` (Link's own),
`none`, or a file in the agent's files folder (`instructions/base.md`).
The model's and the tools' have no source: its file in
`instructions/models/` and what each tool says of itself, so only
their most is set. The repository's is `link` (its `AGENTS.md` files)
or `none`.

isolation.description:
An agent specification's `[isolation]`: the VM a new agent is made in, its
only key a specification may set.

model.description: The model, and how it's asked.

name.description:
The agent's own name, no other: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. A
specification naming another agent is refused.

run.description: How an agent runs on its machine (`[run]`).

schedules.description: Schedule definitions owned by this agent, independent of its harness.

items.description:
A schedule the agent keeps: a message sent to it at a time, as if
from where it goes.

storage.description:
Where an agent would keep each of its collections (its specification's
`[storage]`): a place's name each, a request its machine has the
last word on. A harness from outside Link keeps its own conversations
however it does.

additionalProperties.description:
A tool's opinions (`[tools]` for every tool, `[tool.<name>]` for one).
Link's tools' keys are typed; a tool from outside Link may have keys
of its own ([`Tool::other`]).

tool.description: Each tool's own, by its name (`memory`).

propertyNames.description: A tool's name, read as the name it has today

tools.description:
A tool's opinions (`[tools]` for every tool, `[tool.<name>]` for one).
Link's tools' keys are typed; a tool from outside Link may have keys
of its own ([`Tool::other`]).

turns.description: How long a turn may go on.

version.description:
A whole number of yours, to say which revision of the specification this
is; Link reads nothing from it.

window.description: How much of the model's window a turn fills.

x-link-generator: Generated by link-actions-surfaces from the module declarations: change those and regenerate, never this file.
